name: Containerization Conventions
description: This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on containerization so output stays consistent and easy to review.
content:
This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on containerization so output stays consistent and easy to review.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Validate containerization outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
2. When containerization decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
3. When multiple containerization strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
4. Document any non-obvious containerization decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
5. Prefer explicit, readable containerization solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
6. Prefer the simplest containerization approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
7. Surface known limitations of a chosen containerization approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
8. Keep containerization changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
9. Check that containerization terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
10. Re-check edge cases relevant to containerization (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting containerization assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid mixing unrelated containerization concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of containerization correctness.
- Avoid introducing new containerization abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these containerization guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
